title: Disney+ Prices Are Going Up: Don’t Miss the “Coming Up Next” on Your Bill!
part1:
News that Disney+ is raising prices may start tense music in your mind. It may make your home budget feel tense. Before you hold your wallet and think, “Not my subscription fees again,” pause. The new U.S. prices do not mean everyone’s bill rises on the same day. The price is the star. The calendar is a surprising co-star.

First, look at the numbers that affect your wallet. The monthly ad plan on its own will rise from $11.99 to $12.49. That is a $0.50 increase. The monthly Premium plan on its own will rise from $18.99 to $21.49. That is a $2.50 increase. The yearly price for the Premium plan on its own is changing too. People who pay by the year should take note.
part2:
Now the story has two paths. New subscribers get the new prices first. People who already subscribe get them later, in a future billing cycle. Each current subscriber’s change date depends on their billing cycle. You may watch the same show on the same night as someone else. Still, your new price may have a different “release date.”

The price-rise headline is a preview sent to everyone. But the main story starts on your bill on a different day for each person. It is too soon to jump to the ending. You may ask, “The news is out. Does my price change today?” First, check if you are a new subscriber or already had a subscription. Then check your billing cycle.

The price list tells you how much you will pay. Look at it with when you signed up and your billing cycle. Then you can see when the change starts for you. We should invite the calendar to the home budget meeting, not just the calculator.
part3:
Now many people ask, “So why are prices going up?” But we do not have a clear answer here. The Disney+ U.S. pricing page does not clearly say why Disney made this change. The Reuters report we checked does not clearly say either. According to Reuters, Disney did not answer a request for comment right away.

The numbers are there, but our sources do not give the reason. We should not write a script based on guesses to fill the gap. If you are checking your subscription costs, look at three things together: how much, when, and how much of the reason has been explained. Next, check not only when your favorite shows will be ready to watch. Also check when you are due to be charged.
in_one_line: Disney+’s U.S. price increases start with new subscribers. Existing customers get the new prices on different billing cycles.
